titleStmt.title: Kephalaia of the Teacher, edition page 48: diplomatic and Leiden transcription

sourceDesc.bibl: Kephalaia (Manichäische Handschriften der Staatlichen Museen Berlin), ed. H. J. Polotsky and A. Böhlig, Stuttgart: Kohlhammer, 48. Restorations, sublinear dots, gap counts and corrections are the editors'.

encodingDesc.p: EpiDoc. Read by eye from the page image; gap counts, sublinear dots and supralinear stroke extents verified by measurement on the image. A supralinear stroke is marked on every letter it covers by at least half its width. Spaces are the edition's word division. Facsimile zones are measured line centres. The editors' German statements are not transcribed: each is mapped to an id of the controlled vocabulary data/kephalaia/editorial_vocabulary.json and carried as @ana (ed: statements in the text, app: apparatus footnotes, tr: categories of the transcriber's commentary).

div.p: The framed manuscript page number [ⲙⲏ] (top left) is printed in restoration brackets with a bar above and below as the frame. Seven illegible dots at the line start (543–702), thirteen at the line end (961–1277). Dot under ϥ of ⲁⲣⲁϥ (881, left of the descender). No strokes. Reconcile flags on this page are explained by faint dots: of area < 6, or too pale to reach the < 130 ink threshold at all (ll. 11, 22, 23, 33 mostly), and by dot rows at the zone centre (ll. 5, 12, 13). Single sublinear dots it misses for size: 20 ⲝ (area 2), 31 ⲣ (area 3). Every dot was counted on the 4× sheets.

Seven illegible dots at the line start (543–701), four after ⲡ (950–1030), two at the line end (1334, 1360). Measured stroke over ϩⲙ (859–883, pixel row 335): ϩ 50 %, ⲙ 67 %, encoded on both. Dots under ⲡ of [ⲙ]ⲡⲕⲁϩ (1101, area 3, visible at 4×) and ⲙ of ⲙⲡⲕⲉ[ⲕⲉ] (1198).
